articles.title: The Growing Role of Large Language Models in Arthroplasty Manuscripts: High-Productivity Authors Lead the Way.
articles.authors: Sahhar M, Lewis AM, Achilova F, Singh M, Nassar JE, Callanan T, et al.
articles.population: Original research articles from six arthroplasty journals
articles.outcomes: Proportion of articles with detectable large language model involvement; associations with author productivity, geographic origin and citation impact
articles.take_home: Use of large language models in arthroplasty research increased significantly from less than 4% in 2018-2021 to 20% in 2025, with the most productive authors using these tools more often. The increase appears driven by research efficiency rather than language barriers, as authors from non-English-speaking countries did not use these tools more frequently.

articles.title: Preoperative Factors Associated With Achieving Patient Acceptable Symptom State After Robot-Assisted Total Hip Arthroplasty Differ According to the Outcome Measure Used.
articles.authors: Coulomb R, Pradel S, Alsuwaidi M, Marquant A, Tallet L, Kouyoumdjian P
articles.study_type: Single-centre retrospective study based on prospective cohort
articles.population: Patients undergoing robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient-acceptable symptom state measured by Numeric Rating Scale for pain, Oxford Hip Score, Harris Hip Score, and Forgotten Joint Score at 12 months post-operatively
articles.take_home: Different factors before surgery predict good outcomes after robot-assisted hip replacement depending on which outcome measure is used. Factors like absence of lower back pain and certain pelvic measurements predicted good results across all measures, but factors like pain levels, age, and smoking status predicted success differently depending on the measure chosen.

articles.title: The knee-ankle link: impact of knee varus severity on distal joint malalignment and concomitant pathologies.
articles.authors: Lee KB, Lee DY
articles.population: Studies examining relationship between knee varus deformity and distal joint alignment or ankle pathologies
articles.outcomes: Association between knee varus severity and ankle osteoarthritis, talar tilt, hindfoot alignment and concomitant ankle pathologies
articles.take_home: Severe knee varus (greater than 10 degrees) is linked to increased risk of ankle osteoarthritis and changes in the foot and ankle position. However, people's bodies adapt differently to this problem, so treatment approaches need to be tailored to individual patients rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach.

articles.title: Ten-year clinical outcomes of modular unlinked bicompartmental knee arthroplasty using an onlay-type patellofemoral arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Baba R, Maeda T, Iwasaki K, Onodera T, Kondo E, Iwasaki N, et al.
articles.population: Patients with bicompartmental knee osteoarthritis undergoing modular unlinked bicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 72 patients (73 knees); 52 knees remained in follow-up at 10 years
articles.outcomes: Knee range of motion (mean 134.5 degrees), Knee Society Score (mean 115.8 points), Japanese Knee Osteoarthritis Measure (improved from 37.5 to 20.7 points), radiographic findings, and postoperative complications
articles.take_home: This combined knee replacement procedure for arthritis in two compartments of the knee showed good results at 10 years, with patients maintaining good movement and function and no implants loosening. Four knees needed further surgery for complications, but none required conversion to full knee replacement.

articles.title: National Case Volume and Economic Burden of Inpatient Revision Hip Arthroplasty for Aseptic Loosening: Trends and Future Projections from 2012 to 2032.
articles.authors: Pisharody VA, Nour G, Chowdary AR, Ross B, Erens GA, Wilson JM, et al.
articles.study_type: National database analysis with cost projections
articles.population: Patients admitted to hospital for revision hip replacement due to aseptic loosening (prosthetic loosening)
articles.outcomes: Annual incidence of revision hip procedures, average cost per admission, total national costs, projected costs to 2032
articles.take_home: The average cost per revision hip replacement for loosening has risen from about £23,000 to £25,000 between 2012 and 2022, and is expected to reach about £29,000 by 2032. Hospital admissions for these procedures fell during the pandemic and have not fully recovered.

articles.title: Projected Case Volume and Economic Burden of Knee Aseptic Loosening in Inpatient Total Knee Arthroplasty in the United States.
articles.authors: Pisharody VA, Nour G, Chowdary AR, Ross B, Erens GA, Premkumar A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis with cost projection modelling
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over admitted for revision knee replacement surgery due to aseptic loosening in the United States
articles.outcomes: Annual incidence and inpatient costs of revision knee replacement for aseptic loosening; projected volume and costs to 2032
articles.take_home: Aseptic loosening requiring repeat knee replacement surgery is becoming more common and costly, with admissions projected to nearly double from 2012 levels to over 30,000 per year by 2032. The total annual cost of treating this complication in the United States is expected to reach approximately one billion dollars by 2032.

articles.title: Knee ligament reconstruction reinforced with FiberTape(R): Versatility in indications and safety profile of 381 cases with a mean follow up of 8 years.
articles.authors: Mabrouk A, Risebury M, Yasen S
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of prospectively maintained database
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee ligament reconstruction with suture tape reinforcement
articles.sample_size: 381 cases (234 anterior cruciate ligament, 92 multi-ligament with ACL involvement, 55 other ligament injuries)
articles.outcomes: Knee stability on KT-1000 arthrometer, range of motion, KOOS score, Lysholm score, Tegner activity score, complications and re-rupture rates
articles.take_home: Knee ligament reconstruction reinforced with high-strength suture tape produced good results with significant improvements in knee stability and function lasting 8 years, with only 3.7% experiencing complications including a 2.1% re-rupture rate in anterior cruciate ligament cases. This reinforcement technique was safe and effective across different types of knee ligament injuries.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Regenerative Therapies for Hip Cartilage Lesions and Their Outcomes.
articles.authors: Woodhouse B, Patel R, Hulme C, Kuiper JH, Rix L, Nandra R, et al.
articles.population: Young, active patients with hip cartilage lesions
articles.outcomes: Modified Harris Hip Score (functional outcome); conversion to total hip replacement (failure); THA-free survival rates
articles.take_home: Cell-based and scaffold-assisted treatments for hip cartilage lesions produced better functional improvements than simpler repair techniques like microfracture. Larger defects and older age were associated with worse outcomes and higher rates of needing hip replacement surgery.

articles.title: Finding the Sweet Spot: A Mixed-Effects Analysis of Four Tourniquet Strategies and Blood Conservation in 15,394 Primary Total Knee Arthroplasties.
articles.authors: Mallett KE, Weinblatt AI, Ondek NT, Oettl FC, Lan R, Lyman S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis with mixed-effects regression modelling
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Perioperative haemoglobin drop, calculated blood loss, and postoperative transfusion requirement
articles.take_home: Using a tourniquet from the start of surgery until cementation was associated with the best blood conservation in knee replacement surgery. Not using a tourniquet increased blood loss and the need for blood transfusion, though the absolute difference was small when tranexamic acid was used.

articles.title: Four general-purpose large language models (ChatGPT-5, Claude 4, Grok 4 and Gemini 2.5) show comparable performance in specialised total knee arthroplasty clinical questions.
articles.authors: Pujol O, Ferrer R, Coelho A, Oettl FC, Zsidai B, Leal-Blanquet J, et al.
articles.population: Specialised total knee arthroplasty clinical questions from the World Expert Meeting in Arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Performance scores on QUEST rating system (1-5 scale) across accuracy, comprehensiveness, trust and currency dimensions; subjective selection of best responses
articles.take_home: Four large language models (ChatGPT-5, Claude 4, Grok 4 and Gemini 2.5) all performed well when answering specialist knee replacement questions, with scores ranging from 4.62 to 4.77 out of 5. No single model was clearly best across all areas, though Claude 4 was subjectively chosen most often by doctors as giving the best answer.

articles.title: Feasibility and accuracy of intraoperative 3D surface scanning to assess femoral component alignment relative to the native distal femoral articular surface in total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Rath B, Huber T, Kamper M, Beckmann J, Hirschmann MT, Hammer N, et al.
articles.population: Post-mortem knee joints from donors
articles.outcomes: 3D scanning accuracy (~0.2 mm), scan time (40-60 seconds), 3D model creation time (3 minutes average), surface conformity between native anatomy and femoral component, accuracy of landmark-based versus marker-based registration
articles.take_home: Handheld 3D surface scanning during knee replacement surgery can quickly and accurately capture the natural shape of the knee joint with millimetre-level precision. The technique was feasible in this controlled laboratory study, but further testing in actual patients is needed before it can be used routinely in surgery.

articles.title: Palpable ankle landmarks provide reliable measures for tibial component coronal alignment in total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Porteous A, Beaumont O, Blucher N, Platt N, Fletcher J
articles.study_type: Radiographic measurement study with reliability analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Angles between tibial axis and ankle landmarks (lateral malleolus, medial malleolus, lateral talus border); inter- and intra-rater reliability of measurements
articles.take_home: Surgeons can use easily felt ankle bone landmarks during knee replacement surgery to position the tibial component reliably without needing expensive navigation or robotic systems. The study found consistent angles between the shin bone axis and ankle landmarks that define safe alignment limits.

articles.title: Collar-Calcar Contact Reduces Risk for Early Periprosthetic Fracture and Subsidence in Dorr Type C Femora Using Collared, Fully Hydroxyapatite-Coated, Cementless Stems.
articles.authors: Navarro JAM, Miura Y, Oinuma K, Ninomiya T
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip replacement through direct anterior approach with Dorr type C femora
articles.sample_size: 387 hips with Dorr C femora (from 6,107 total procedures reviewed)
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic fracture and implant subsidence within 90 days postoperatively
articles.take_home: Hip replacements with collared stems that made full contact with the bone had significantly lower rates of fracture and subsidence compared to those with gaps, suggesting proper positioning of the collar against bone is important for stability.

articles.title: Reduced Wound Complications with Absorbable Deep Dermal Staples in Direct Anterior Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Abuoqab L, Rice SW, Crawford DA
articles.population: Patients undergoing direct anterior approach total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 703 consecutive primary cases (357 absorbable staples, 346 barbed sutures)
articles.outcomes: Wound complication rates and return to operating room for wound issues
articles.take_home: Absorbable deep dermal staples reduced wound complications to 2.8% compared to 8.1% with barbed sutures alone, though patients with higher BMI remained at increased risk regardless of closure method.

articles.title: Distribution of Total Knee Arthroplasty Periprosthetic Infection Care in the United States: Reported from the American Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Elmenawi KA, Zaniletti I, Poilvache H, Hannon CP, Abdel MP, Bedard NA
articles.study_type: Registry analysis of surgical volume distribution
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty for periprosthetic joint infection in the United States
articles.sample_size: 45,914 knee periprosthetic joint infection surgeries performed by 8,658 surgeons across 1,366 institutions between 2012 and 2022
articles.outcomes: Proportion of surgeries performed at high, medium and low-volume institutions and by high, medium and low-volume surgeons
articles.take_home: Most knee infection surgeries in the US are currently managed by surgeons and hospitals with low experience of this specific procedure, with only 4% treated by high-volume specialists at high-volume centres. Concentrating all such care at specialist centres may not be practical or sustainable.

articles.title: Preoperative Gait Analysis Predicts Surgical Candidacy and Clinical Severity in Hip Osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Hu J, Zhong W, Liu C, Yang X, Cui H, Cheng H
articles.study_type: Single-centre observational study with matched controls
articles.population: Patients with hip osteoarthritis undergoing total hip replacement, and matched non-operative controls
articles.outcomes: Preoperative gait parameters (step length, knee range of motion, gait cycles) and their association with joint damage, pain, function, and 12-month postoperative outcomes
articles.take_home: How patients walk before hip replacement surgery can help predict how well they will function after the operation. Gait analysis provides useful additional information alongside standard X-rays and questionnaires to help doctors decide who needs surgery and what results to expect.

articles.title: Linking Joint-Specific Recovery to Overall Health Through Patient-Reported Outcome Measures: A Propensity-Score Matched Cohort Study in Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Park J, Miley EN, Zhong X, Gray CF
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty or total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Changes in disease-specific scores (HOOS JR/KOOS JR) correlated with overall health measures including physical health, mental health, and quality of life at one year post-operatively
articles.take_home: Improvements in hip and knee function after joint replacement are moderately to strongly linked with improvements in physical health, but only weakly linked with mental health and quality of life. Both hip and knee replacements showed similar patterns of correlation between joint-specific recovery and overall health.

articles.title: 'Overall pain' is strongly associated with patient satisfaction: An item-level longitudinal analysis of the Oxford Knee Score in total and unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tay ML, Rahardja R, Farrington WJ, Kawaguchi K, Young SW
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis of registry data
articles.population: Patients who had total or unicompartmental knee replacement surgery
articles.sample_size: 9384 total knee arthroplasties and 2424 unicompartmental knee arthroplasties
articles.outcomes: Association between individual Oxford Knee Score questions and patient satisfaction from 6 months to 15 years after surgery; Patient Acceptable Symptom State thresholds
articles.take_home: The question about overall pain was the single strongest predictor of patient satisfaction after knee replacement at all time points up to 15 years. This suggests that managing pain should be a key focus for achieving satisfied patients after this surgery.

articles.title: Anterior opening-wedge high tibial osteotomy for restoring posterior tibial slope in PCL insufficiency and genu recurvatum: A narrative review.
articles.authors: Cohen D, Ambrosini L, Dickschas J, van Heerwaarden R, Ollivier M, Musahl V
articles.population: Patients with posterior cruciate ligament insufficiency and genu recurvatum
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes, graft survival, tibial slope correction, complications including hinge fractures and patella baja
articles.take_home: Anterior opening-wedge high tibial osteotomy can restore normal tibial slope in patients with PCL insufficiency or genu recurvatum, with studies showing slope improvements of 9 to 24 degrees and 70-90% achieving good-to-excellent results. This procedure may help prevent ligament graft failure and reduce pain and instability, though it carries risks including fractures and loss of knee extension.

articles.title: Isolated medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction provides similar outcomes in patients with increased versus normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove distance.
articles.authors: Vincent JB, Erard J, Free M, Faure F, Batailler C, Lustig S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with recurrent patellar dislocation undergoing isolated medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 121 consecutive patients (90 with normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove distance, 31 with increased distance)
articles.outcomes: International Knee Documentation Committee score at minimum 24 months follow-up; functional improvement; complication rates; recurrence of instability
articles.take_home: Patients with increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove distance had similar clinical outcomes to those with normal distance after isolated ligament reconstruction, with no difference in complications or recurrence. This suggests that increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove distance alone should not determine whether additional bone surgery is needed.

articles.title: Acoustic evaluation by artificial intelligence for initial press-fit cementless cup fixation in total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Homma Y, Tashiro K, Ohtsu H, Hayashi K, Watari T, Baba T, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement for osteoarthritis or bone death of the femur
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of artificial intelligence in detecting successful press-fit cup fixation using hammering sound analysis; Model B (sound plus patient details) achieved 96.5% accuracy
articles.take_home: An artificial intelligence system that listens to hammering sounds during hip replacement surgery could accurately tell whether the artificial cup is properly fitted, potentially helping surgeons during the operation. The system worked best when combined with patient information, achieving very high accuracy levels.

articles.title: Impact of T4-L1-Hip Axis Normalization on Outcomes and Complications in Adult Spinal Deformity.
articles.authors: Mohanty S, Sardar ZM, Reyes JL, Hassan FM, Kelly MP, Coury JR, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing surgery for spinal deformity with fusion of more than 6 levels of the spine
articles.outcomes: Mechanical complications including implant-related reoperations and proximal junctional failure; patient-reported outcomes using Scoliosis Research Society and Oswestry Disability Index scores
articles.take_home: Getting the spinal alignment just right during surgery reduced the risk of implant failure and complications, but achieving ideal alignment did not improve patients' pain or disability scores. Both undercorrection and overcorrection of the spine's alignment increased complication risks.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of analgesic techniques in total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and network meta-analysis of more than 100 randomized studies incorporating minimal clinically important difference.
articles.authors: Cheok T, Berman M, Jordan W, Beveridge A, Smith T, Morrison C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Pain scores at 12 hours and day 1 after surgery, opioid consumption within 24 hours, time to first mobilization, hospital length of stay
articles.take_home: No pain relief technique made a meaningful difference to pain on day 1 after hip replacement surgery. Intrathecal morphine and a combination of iliopsoas block with periarticular injection did reduce opioid use, whilst intrathecal morphine and pericapsular nerve block reduced hospital stays.

articles.title: "Two Strikes, You're Out": Contemporary Revision Patterns Following Instability after Posterior and Anterior Approach Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Driscoll DA, Burgio C, Viggiano M, Yared T, Trenchfield D, Sokrab R, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty and experienced dislocation
articles.sample_size: 285 patients with dislocation out of 40,315 primary THAs (0.7%)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery for instability following dislocation events, analysed by number of dislocations and timing of instability
articles.take_home: The risk of needing revision surgery after hip dislocation increases significantly after a second dislocation (94% risk), with little additional increase after three or more dislocations. Dislocations occurring more than 90 days after surgery were more likely to require revision than those happening earlier.

articles.title: Magnetic three-dimensional dynamic tracking of total knee arthroplasty can detect rotational movements within one degree accuracy in most configurations: new principles for medical imaging.
articles.authors: Naudi S, May O, Fouilleron N, Kheddar A, Dutrieux S, Mehdi N
articles.population: Total knee arthroplasty implants of varying sizes
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of rotational tracking within one degree for femoral and tibial components across different implant sizes and knee positions
articles.take_home: A new magnetic tracking device called Kneematics can accurately measure the rotation of knee replacement implants in the lab, detecting movements within one degree in over 90% of test configurations. This early laboratory work suggests the device could eventually be useful for tracking how knee replacements move in patients.

articles.title: The effect of hip abductor or external rotator strength on dynamic knee valgus in healthy subjects-a systematic review with partial meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Cashman G, White C, Stephens R, Hoggs-Johnson S, Kissel J
articles.population: Healthy asymptomatic subjects
articles.outcomes: Association between hip abductor and external rotator strength and dynamic knee valgus measured by dynamometry and kinematic analysis
articles.take_home: The review found little evidence that weak hip muscles cause increased knee valgus in healthy people, with most studies showing no significant link between hip strength and knee position. This suggests that prescribing hip strengthening exercises specifically to prevent knee problems may not be justified by the current evidence in healthy individuals.

articles.title: Full and Half Cup-Cage Reconstruction of Major Acetabular Defects: A Concise Follow-up, at 10 Years, of a Previous Report.
articles.authors: Berdis GE, Carstens MF, Larson DR, Perry KI, Taunton MJ, Bedard NA, et al.
articles.population: Patients with major acetabular bone defects undergoing reconstruction with cup-cage constructs
articles.outcomes: Implant survival, clinical outcomes, and radiographic findings at 10-year follow-up
articles.take_home: This 10-year follow-up study evaluated how well full and half cup-cage reconstructions performed in treating major acetabular defects, providing longer-term outcomes data for this surgical technique.

articles.title: Nontraumatic Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: An Update.
articles.authors: Mont MA, Smitterberg CW, Jones LC, Goodman SB, Lieberman JR, Parvizi J, et al.
articles.population: Patients under 50 years of age with persistent hip pain and nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head
articles.outcomes: Detection of osteonecrosis using imaging; progression based on lesion size and location; effectiveness of joint-preserving procedures versus total hip replacement
articles.take_home: Nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head should be suspected in younger patients with persistent hip pain and normal X-rays. MRI is the best imaging test for early detection, and joint-preserving treatments work best before the femoral head collapses, after which hip replacement becomes the most reliable option.

articles.title: Optimising femoral head extraction to preserve the tensor fasciae latae in direct anterior hip arthroplasty: a technical note.
articles.authors: Ongkosit C
articles.study_type: Technical note describing a surgical method
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip arthroplasty via direct anterior approach
articles.sample_size: 63 procedures (31 total hip arthroplasties and 32 bipolar hemiarthroplasties)
articles.outcomes: Tensor fasciae latae muscle damage during femoral head extraction; damage score of 0 in 28 total hip arthroplasty hips and all 32 hemiarthroplasty hips
articles.take_home: A new step-by-step technique using a Schanz pin and corkscrew during hip replacement surgery significantly reduced injury to the tensor fasciae latae muscle, with most patients having no damage to this muscle.

articles.title: Survivorship of the C-Stem in cement-in-cement revision hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yadav AK, As-Sultany M, Siney P, Paul I, Rajpura A, Kay P
articles.population: Patients undergoing cement-in-cement femoral revision hip arthroplasty with C-Stem implant
articles.outcomes: Stem revision rates, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, radiological outcomes, complications
articles.take_home: The C-Stem in cement-in-cement revision hip surgery had an 86% survival rate at 8 years with only 11.8% needing further revision. This less invasive technique appears to work well in carefully selected patients, with no cases needing revision due to stem loosening.

articles.title: Optimising spherical periacetabular osteotomy: a strategy to minimise leg shortening.
articles.authors: Nishiwaki T, Ishikura H, Masuyama Y, Fujita S
articles.population: Patients with hip dysplasia undergoing spherical periacetabular osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Leg length change, acetabular correction angles, fixation type (contact versus non-contact), bone fragment stability
articles.take_home: When the cut bone surfaces remain in direct contact after surgery, patients experience minimal leg shortening (average 0.3 mm), whilst non-contact fixation causes greater shortening (average 6.1 mm). Better fixation techniques are needed for cases where bone surfaces do not stay in contact.
